options.text: I naturally start conversations and build relationships.
I keep pushing when progress is slower than expected.
I make sure details and follow-ups do not get missed.
I act on opportunities without needing much prompting.
I stay calm when conversations become difficult.
I am comfortable taking the lead in a discussion.
I adjust quickly when circumstances change.
I stay productive without someone checking on me.
I enjoy meeting and talking with new people.
I reliably finish commitments I make.
I create momentum when there is no obvious next step.
I can keep working a lead after several setbacks.
I like keeping records and next steps organized.
I can ask directly for a decision when the time is right.
I recover quickly from rejection.
I find another approach when the first one fails.
I set my own priorities and get moving.
I build rapport quickly with different personalities.
I notice unfinished responsibilities and close the loop.
I pursue worthwhile opportunities proactively.
I stay with important goals for a long time.
I am comfortable respectfully challenging someone.
I keep a clear system for people I need to follow up with.
I remain level-headed under pressure.
I adapt my communication to the person in front of me.
I can work independently for long stretches.
I enjoy frequent interaction throughout my day.
I follow through even on tasks nobody is checking.
I look for productive work instead of waiting for assignments.
I keep trying after hearing no.
I am comfortable guiding a conversation toward a decision.
I keep information organized so others can rely on it.

scenarios.prompt: You finish your planned work earlier than expected. What are you most likely to do?

options.text: Review active opportunities and choose useful follow-up to advance.
Clean up records and make sure every next step is documented.
Reach out to people and create additional conversations.
Review recent results and adjust tomorrow's plan.

scenarios.prompt: A prospect has been polite but noncommittal after several conversations. What feels most natural?

options.text: Ask a direct question to understand what is preventing a decision.
Keep a thoughtful follow-up cadence and stay patient.
Try a different communication angle based on what you have learned.
Make sure the notes and next action are clear before moving on.

scenarios.prompt: You have a difficult conversation and the other person becomes irritated. What do you tend to do?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on understanding the concern.
Address the issue directly while staying respectful.
Change the approach and see whether another angle works better.
Give the situation some space and follow up at an appropriate time.

scenarios.prompt: You have several follow-ups due and a new opportunity appears. What do you naturally prioritize?

options.text: Handle the time-sensitive new opportunity, then return to the list.
Work the committed follow-ups first unless the new item is truly urgent.
Quickly rank everything by potential impact and work from the top.
Contact the people most likely to respond and build momentum.

Field Agent.prompt: You knock on a door and the homeowner seems skeptical about why you are there. What feels most natural?

options.text: Introduce myself simply, acknowledge the interruption, and ask a low-pressure question.
Be direct about why I am there and quickly determine whether there is interest.
Read their reaction and adjust my tone before asking anything further.
Respect the hesitation, leave a clear way to reconnect, and document the follow-up.

Field Agent.prompt: You have been knocking for an hour with very few conversations. What do you naturally do?

options.text: Keep going and focus on completing the activity I committed to.
Change my opening or approach and test whether response improves.
Review the route and move toward the highest-priority properties.
Reset my energy and make the next interaction feel like the first one.

Field Agent.prompt: You meet a homeowner who is not ready to talk but may be interested later. What do you do?

options.text: Ask permission for a specific follow-up and record it immediately.
Try to understand one useful detail before ending the conversation.
Leave the door open and make sure they feel comfortable reconnecting.
Set a follow-up and continue working the rest of the area.

Acquisitions.prompt: A homeowner is interested but says they need time to think. What feels most natural?

options.text: Ask what specifically they still need to think through.
Agree on a specific follow-up time and keep the relationship moving.
Revisit what they want and make sure the conversation still addresses it.
Give them room while writing down what matters for the next conversation.

Acquisitions.prompt: Several homeowners are due for follow-up and a new person wants to talk. What do you do?

options.text: Quickly judge what is most urgent and reorder the day.
Respond to the new person quickly, then return to the follow-ups you already promised.
Stick to the follow-up list unless the new person truly needs you right now.
Make contact right away because a timely reply matters.

Acquisitions.prompt: A homeowner strongly disagrees with the number you shared. What is your first instinct?

options.text: Ask questions to understand what is driving the reaction.
Go back to what they want and see whether another path still helps.
Explain the reasoning clearly and ask what would help the conversation continue.
Keep the relationship intact and set a thoughtful follow-up.

Virtual Closer.prompt: An offer was sent two days ago and the seller has not responded. What feels most natural?

options.text: Call with a direct but low-pressure question about what is holding things up.
Use a planned call and text sequence and continue until there is clarity.
Change the message angle to make it easier for the seller to respond.
Review the prior conversation first so the follow-up is highly relevant.

Virtual Closer.prompt: The seller wants a price above what you are allowed to offer. What do you do?

options.text: Explore the reasons behind the number and stay within the approved range.
Look for concerns other than price that may open another path.
Clearly explain the limit and escalate only when there is a justified reason.
Keep the conversation moving without promising something you cannot authorize.

Virtual Closer.prompt: A seller seems close to signing but wants to see the property with someone first. What do you do?

options.text: Set a clear local appointment and define what happens immediately afterward.
Ask what they hope the visit will resolve so the appointment has a purpose.
Coordinate the appointment quickly and keep ownership of the follow-up.
Confirm the concern, schedule the visit, and keep momentum without pressure.

checks.text: I sometimes need a reminder for something I intended to finish.
I can stay productive when nobody is checking on me.
Rejection can occasionally affect my energy.
I enjoy initiating conversations with people I do not know.
I usually remember every commitment without any system or reminder.
I occasionally work better when expectations are clearly reinforced.
A difficult interaction rarely affects me at all.
I sometimes prefer familiar people over starting conversations with strangers.

work_sample_prompt: A homeowner texts you: "That's way lower than I expected." Write what you'd say back, or how you'd handle this response. No real estate experience is needed.
voice_prompt: Optional: record up to 60 seconds introducing yourself to a homeowner who asked about selling. You can skip this. No real estate experience is needed.
